# Comparison to n8n

Covers dimension 14. Sources referenced in [citations.md](../citations.md).
n8n analysis at `research/n8n/` provides the benchmark.

---

## Feature-by-Feature Comparison

| Dimension | Activepieces | n8n | Assessment | Sources |
|-----------|-------------|-----|------------|---------|
| **License** | MIT (OSI-approved) | Sustainable Use License (not OSI) | AP stronger | [3], n8n analysis |
| **Self-hosting** | Docker, Docker Compose | Docker, K8s, npm | Equivalent | [8][9][10] |
| **CLI execution** | UNSANDBOXED mode: full shell access | Code node: JS/Python | AP equivalent (mode-dependent) | [6] |
| **Credential isolation** | 256-bit encryption, no retrieval API | AES256, no retrieval API | Equivalent | [14], n8n analysis |
| **Scheduling** | Cron (Quartz), daily/weekly/monthly | Cron, interval triggers | Equivalent | Agent B |
| **REST API** | 15 endpoint groups, Bearer auth | CRUD at /rest/*, Bearer auth | Equivalent | [15], n8n analysis |
| **Webhooks** | GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, Basic/Header auth | Full HTTP, multiple auth | Equivalent | [13] |
| **Execution history** | Per-step I/O, 30-day retention | Per-step I/O, configurable retention | Equivalent | [11][12] |
| **Retry** | 4 retries over ~4 min, per-step | Configurable retries with backoff | n8n stronger | [18], n8n analysis |
| **AI/LLM** | Universal AI pieces, MCP servers | 70+ LangChain nodes, MCP client+server | n8n stronger | [19], n8n analysis |
| **Integrations** | 200-450+ pieces | 400+ nodes + ~5,800 community | n8n stronger | [2][21][22] |
| **GitHub stars** | 21,600 | 150,000+ | n8n larger | [2], n8n analysis |
| **Ease of setup** | G2: 9.1/10 | G2: 7.9/10 | AP stronger | [21][22] |
| **Performance** | 95 req/s (sandboxed benchmark) | Faster in comparative tests | n8n stronger | [16][21] |
| **Workflow topology** | Linear (one trigger per flow) | Graph (multiple triggers, branching) | n8n stronger | [22] |

## Performance Comparison

Third-party benchmarks show a performance gap that varies by workload [21][22]:

| Test | n8n | Activepieces | Ratio | Source |
|------|-----|-------------|-------|--------|
| Simple webhook task | 0.5-1s | ~15s | 15-30x slower | [21] |
| 77 concurrent requests | ~20s total | ~2 min total | ~6x slower | [21] |
| Optimized throughput | 220+ exec/s | Lower | — | [21] |

The gap narrows significantly under concurrent workloads (~6x) compared to
simple sequential tasks (15-30x).

**Context:** The performance gap is attributed to Activepieces' process-per-task
isolation model [21]. The `UNSANDBOXED` mode was not benchmarked in these
comparisons. Activepieces' own benchmarks show 95.1 req/s in `SANDBOX_CODE_ONLY`
mode [16] and up to 336.6 req/s with scaled workers [16].

**Important caveat:** These benchmarks test sandboxed multi-tenant modes. For a
personal workstation running UNSANDBOXED mode, the performance gap may be
smaller. No published benchmarks compare UNSANDBOXED Activepieces to n8n
directly.

## Integration Depth

n8n's integrations are deeper per connector [22]:

> "n8n's HubSpot node supported 12 trigger types and 20+ actions. ActivePieces'
> HubSpot piece supported 3 triggers and 8 actions." [22]

For the PA use case, this matters less — domain logic lives in CLI tools, not
built-in integrations. The workflow engine primarily needs to execute scripts and
pass data between steps.

## Pricing Comparison

| Plan | Activepieces | n8n | Source |
|------|-------------|-----|--------|
| Cloud free | 1,000 tasks/month, 2 flows | 14-day trial only | [21] |
| Cloud entry | $25/month (unlimited tasks, 10 flows) | $24/month (2,500 exec, 5 workflows) | [21] |
| Self-hosted | Free, unlimited | Free, unlimited | [21][22] |

Activepieces' flat-rate pricing with unlimited tasks eliminates usage anxiety
[22]. n8n's execution-based pricing counts entire workflows as 1 execution
(not per-step like Zapier).

---

## Workflow Model

| Aspect | Activepieces | n8n | Source |
|--------|-------------|-----|--------|
| Builder style | Step-based vertical | Node-based canvas | [21][22] |
| Triggers per flow | One | Multiple | [21][22] (inferred from linear builder model) |
| Branching | Linear with conditionals | Complex graph topology | [22] |
| Mental model | Sequential pipeline | Directed graph | [21][22] |

n8n's node-based canvas allows more complex workflow topologies [22]. Activepieces'
step-based builder is simpler but more constrained — one trigger per flow limits
composability.

## Where Activepieces Is Stronger

1. **Licensing:** MIT is unambiguously open source; n8n's SUL has commercial
   restrictions [3][21]
2. **Ease of setup:** G2 9.1 vs 7.9 — lower barrier for non-technical users
   [21][22]
3. **MCP integration:** All pieces auto-exposed as MCP servers [2][24]
4. **Cloud pricing:** Free tier + unlimited tasks on paid plans [21]
5. **SOC 2 Type II:** Certified [22]; n8n's compliance status different

## Where n8n Is Stronger

1. **Performance:** 15-30x faster in sandbox mode benchmarks [21]
2. **AI/LLM:** 70+ LangChain nodes, 12 vector stores, mature agent framework
3. **Integrations:** 400+ official + ~5,800 community nodes
4. **Integration depth:** More triggers/actions per connector [22]
5. **Workflow complexity:** Multi-trigger, graph-based topology [22]
6. **Community size:** 150k+ vs 21.6k GitHub stars [2]
7. **Maturity:** Founded 2019 vs 2022; $2.5B valuation vs early-stage

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- No UNSANDBOXED mode benchmark comparison exists
- n8n comparison blog post returned CSS only (SPA rendering)
- Integration count varies significantly across sources and time
- Performance benchmarks are from third parties, not controlled experiments
- n8n's AI capabilities are documented from prior research; Activepieces' AI
  claims partially unverified
